newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-McIntosh shares up on takeover talk.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-McIntosh shares up on takeover talk.

text.p: The shares of listed Australian stock broker McIntosh Securities Ltd rose on Thursday on speculation that the company was a takeover target.
McIntosh shares, normally lightly traded, closed four cents higher at a 1996 high of A$1.10 on moderate volume of 84,400.

Market sources said McIntosh was believed to have held talks with a number of overseas brokers in the last six months, including U.S. securities house Merrill Lynch and Co about possible partnerships or joint ventures.
McIntosh chief executive John McGowan said he had no comment on the rumour and a spokesman for Merrill Lynch in Sydney was not available for comment.
McIntosh, co-lead manager of last week's successful float of Orogen Minerals Ltd, is one of only two listed Australian brokers. The other is Hartley Poynton Ltd.

McIntosh, which is 19.9 percent owned by Dutch bank and insurance group Internationale Nederlanden Groep (ING), reported a net profit of A$10.05 million for 1995/96 compared with a net loss of A$7.04 million a year earlier.
ING inherited its McIntosh stake through its takeover of the troubled British investment bank Barings Plc in March 1995.
